newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S., not Germany real problem in fx rates - Sapin.
newsitem.headline: U.S., not Germany real problem in fx rates - Sapin.

text.p: France should tackle the United States and not Germany over currency parities, as the real problem stems from a deliberate U.S. policy to undervalue the dollar, former French Finance Minister Michel Sapin said.

Sapin, who also served as a member of the Bank of France's monetary policy council until 1995, condemned a call by ex-president Valery Giscard d'Estaing for a franc depreciation as endangering the move to a single European currency.
"His reasoning comes from a different era, today you do not decide an exchange rate parity by decree," the Socialist politician said in a newsletter for the grouping Action for Socialist Renewal.

But Europe had to show a real political will to tackle the undervaluation in the dollar. "There is a real American will to keep the dollar undervalued," he said. "It is the Americans we have to address and not the Germans."

"But we cannot do this alone, we must act with other European countries. And that is exactly the aim of creating a single European currency -- reaching a big enough critical mass to tackle the supremacy of the dollar," he said.
Devaluing the franc against the mark would simply force up interest rates and was not the answer. "The fundamental problem is the parity between the euro and the dollar," he said.
